statement:
No blocking or major defect was found. The adapter takes the 375 OR-Library single-machine total weighted tardiness instances (wt40, wt50, wt100; 125 each). It presents each as an ordered assignment: positions are the variables, jobs are the options with capacity one, so every answer is a processing order. It exposes only each job's published p, w and d, relabelled per seed. It scores an order by (Z - V)/(Z - R) cut to [0, 1]. Here V is the total weighted tardiness, R is the published value (wtopt40, wtopt50, wtbest100b), and Z is the exact expected value of a uniformly random order.

I rebuilt the parsing, the objective and the zero point myself from the page text, independently of the adapter, and it agrees everywhere I tested:
- every p, w, d, reference and optimal/best-known flag of all 375 instances;
- 300 answers: the value exactly, the score within 7.3e-16;
- 762 steps of partial evaluation: exact;
- Z within 5.9e-16 of exact rational values on 95 instances, including all 40 that split(env, 16, 24) uses.

Other properties hold too:
- Nothing the learner can observe changes when the reference, zero point, optimal flag or group is altered.
- training=True and training=False build identical objects.
- The per-instance relabelling removes the w/p job order hidden in the wt100 file.
- Every malformed answer scores 0.
- The manifest's hashes, the re-fetched files and the terms statement are accurate.

The source publishes values only, not orders. My own search reaches the published value exactly on 26 of 32 sampled instances, and no rule or search ever goes below one.

Two properties must go with any result reported on this category:
1. One-pass textbook dispatching rules already pass the 0.98 threshold (ATC 0.992 and WMDD 0.993 on the fresh instances), so "held" means that level.
2. The deciding half of the fresh instances is near its ceiling: 9 of 14 instances have R = 0, which the due-date order reaches. The confirming half is a different, high-tardiness regime.
coverage:
Everything was run with nice -n 10, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, python3 -I, one process at a time, each under ulimit -t 59. Total was about 2.5 CPU-minutes. Scripts: <scratch>/fresh/tardiness/audit2/check.py (parts build, priv, relabel, agree, zero_small, zlist, zero, mc, degenerate, split, anchor, align, extra, hashes, after) and audit2/mine/own.py. own.py is my own page and file parser, integer evaluator, exact zero point, rules and search; it imports nothing from the adapter. Outputs are in audit2/mine/ (table.json, zeros_exact.json, rules.json, zlist.json) and the re-fetched files in audit2/refetch/.

The audit2 directory already held files from an earlier attempt. I did not load its cache.pkl, did not reuse its results, and moved its check.py to audit2/earlier_attempt/.

The constructor was run for real (5.4 CPU-s). The later parts rebuild the object around its instance table, which I checked identical in types, dtypes and values; problem(), score() and group() read only that table.

What was checked:
1. I read every line of the module.
2. Monkeypatching: 7 patches of reference, zero, proven and group on 7 instances. The fingerprint covered the view's fields, the start state, candidates/assign/totals over a full construction, evaluate of 3 answers and the meter.
3. Relabelling: seeds, the decode/evaluate/score round trip, rank correlations of file position, and the identity answer under per-instance seeds.
4. Evaluator agreement and partial evaluation, through the view against the slow default AssignProblem._rows and my own increments; meter charges.
5. Zero point:
   - 70 tiny instances (n = 1..7) checked by full enumeration;
   - 95 instances checked by exact counting modulo primes below 2^31 with the Chinese remainder theorem (all k, no complement, no floating point);
   - 3 instances checked by Monte Carlo with 40,000 orders each.
   - 20 malformed answer forms, scored raw and through decode, plus kernel _valid.
6. Split and halves; twins by shared (p, w) multisets, shared runs of six values, and identical p or d multisets.
7. Every number in the anchor and docstring, with my own EDD, WSPT, better-of-two, adjacent-swap descent, ATC (k = 1, 2, 3) and WMDD, over fresh, deciding, confirming and all.
8. Manifest hashes on disk; re-fetch of wtinfo.html, wt40, wt100, wtopt40, wtopt50, wtbest100a, wtbest100b, the directory listing and legal.html with the required user agent. All match the manifest; wt50.txt was not re-fetched, but its hash on disk matches. The package copy has the same 70 file hashes before and after, and no bytecode was written.

Not checked:
- the exact zero point on the other 280 instances (the 95 cover every class and every instance the split uses);
- optimality of the references (not attempted, per the rules);
- search alignment on n = 100 (too costly; checked instead by rules never beating R, with ATC/R median 1.027);
- the learner and rsi6.kernel.run.measure (not run or read). Kernel-style relabelling seeds were reproduced with the tests' crc32 derivation.

Note: the kernel's scalar-search test "no reference in the problem" would flag 60 instances if it were applied to every instance. The flags are R = 0, which equals the False in hard/detail (53 instances), plus 7 chance equalities with a due date. As written it checks only wt100-001, which is not flagged. The decisive test here was byte-identity under monkeypatching.

findings.title: Deciding half near ceiling; the two halves are different due-date regimes
findings.problem: halves(env, split(env,16,24)[1]) gives a deciding half of 14 instances in 3 groups (wt100-tf0.2-rdd0.6, wt50-tf0.2-rdd1.0, wt50-tf0.4-rdd0.8). On 9 of them R = 0 and the due-date order reaches it, scoring exactly 1.0. The confirming half has 10 instances in 2 groups (wt100-tf0.8-rdd0.2, wt50-tf0.6-rdd1.0) with R > 0 on all. A decision on the deciding half therefore rests in effect on the 5 instances of wt50-tf0.4-rdd0.8. Its 'confirmation' is on another regime: low TF favours the due-date order, high TF the w/p order. A disagreement between the halves is therefore not evidence of chance alone. The docstring and the anchor disclose this.
findings.evidence: check.py split: 'deciding half: 14 instances ... R = 0 on 9'; 'confirming half: 10 instances ... R = 0 on 0'. check.py anchor: EDD fresh 0.733 / deciding 0.967 / confirming 0.405; WSPT 0.691 / 0.635 / 0.770. check.py extra: EDD scores exactly 1.0 on all 53 instances with R = 0.
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the adapter: renaming groups to move the hash-ordered split would amount to choosing instances. In any registration that uses this category, state that 9 of the 14 deciding instances are at the due-date-order ceiling, report scores per group as well as per half, and do not read a deciding/confirming disagreement on this category as a failed replication.

findings.title: Threshold 0.98 is below one-pass textbook dispatching rules and was placed using baseline scores on the fresh split
findings.problem: ATC (k = 2) and WMDD are one-pass rules that search nothing. They score 0.992/0.995/0.987 and 0.993/0.995/0.989 on fresh/deciding/confirming, above 0.98. So a capability 'held' at 0.98 is the level of a fixed textbook rule. The value was raised from 0.90 to 0.98 after these rules' scores on the 24 fresh instances were seen, which puts it in the gap between adjacent-swap descent (0.969) and ATC (0.992). No learner result was involved. The anchor states this plainly and every number in it reproduces.
findings.evidence: check.py anchor: descent 0.969/0.994/0.933/0.946; atc2 0.992/0.995/0.987/0.984; wmdd 0.993/0.995/0.989/0.990; ATC k=1 and k=3 0.9958 on the deciding half; 10% above R scores 0.978 on the fresh instances. All match the anchor and docstring to the third decimal.
findings.fix: No change is needed for correctness. Any report of 'held' on tardiness must quote the anchor's sentence that ATC and WMDD exceed the threshold. If the owner wants 'held' to mean better than every listed no-learning rule on every part, the threshold must be at least 0.996, and that has to be decided before any learner result is seen.

findings.title: The kernel's generic scalar search for the reference flags zero references and chance equalities
findings.problem: This concerns the kernel's test, not the adapter. test_problem_carries_no_reference looks for the reference among all scalars of the problem object. On this category R = 0 for 53 instances, and 0 equals the False in hard/detail. On 7 more instances R happens to equal one of the instance's own due dates. Applied beyond instance_ids()[0], the check would report 60 spurious leaks. As written it passes, because wt100-001 is not flagged.
findings.evidence: check.py extra: 'the kernel test's check would flag 60 instances ... first id wt100-001 flagged: False'. check.py priv: R equals one of the instance's own p, w or d on 7 instances, none with R = 0. Under 7 patches of the reference, zero point and flags, every observable stays byte-identical.
findings.fix: In rsi6/tests/test_kernel.py, base the check on byte-identity of the problem when the stored reference is patched (as done here), or exclude boolean arrays and R = 0 from the value search. The adapter needs no change.

evaluator_agreement:
My evaluator is Python integers: C(j) is the running sum of p in the given order and the value is SUM w max(C - d, 0), written from the page text.

- Random and structured answers: 300 answers on wt40-001, wt40-019 (unsolved), wt50-063, wt50-111 (unsolved), wt100-050 and wt100-118 (wtbest100b < wtbest100a). Each instance had 10 random orders and 40 perturbations of EDD, WSPT, ATC, WMDD and descent orders. The problem's evaluate() equals my value exactly (max difference 0). env.score(decode(a)) equals my exact-rational score (Z, R) within 7.3e-16. My scores were 11% at 0 and 89% strictly between 0 and 1.
- Exact score of 1: orders that reach R score exactly 1.0 (wt40-006 at R; EDD on all 53 instances with R = 0).
- Partial evaluation, through the learner's view: 762 steps over 24 partial constructions. candidates() equals AssignProblem._rows (the difference of partial_totals) and my own increments exactly. totals() after assign() equals partial_totals(a), the view's s['tot'], and my value of the prefix.
- Meter charges: start 1, candidates n per variable, assign 1, evaluate n.
- Decode: 150 more random answers confirm decode/evaluate/score consistency. One file order given under two seeds gives the same value and decodes back.
- References: my own parse of wtopt40, wtopt50 and wtbest100b (125 integers each, in file order) equals the adapter's on all 375; so do my unsolved lists from the page (40: {19}; 50: {11,12,14,19,36,44,66,87,88,111}) and the resulting 239 optimal / 136 best known. wtbest100b is below wtbest100a only at 111-114, 116 and 118-120.
- The source publishes values only, no orders, so no published answer could be re-scored. Instead, my insertion-and-swap search reached the published value exactly on 26 of 32 sampled n = 40/50 instances (including unsolved wt50-011) and was never below one. EDD, WSPT, ATC, WMDD and descent are never below the published value on any of the 375. ATC/R medians are 1.028, 1.031 and 1.027 for n = 40, 50, 100. R = 0 exactly when EDD has no tardiness, on all 375.
- Zero point: on 95 instances, the adapter's floating-point formula is within 5.86e-16 relative of my exact rational value (median 1.4e-16). On 70 tiny instances enumerated over all n! orders, the worst error is 2.6e-16, and my routine equals the enumeration. The 40,000-order Monte Carlo means are within 1.25 standard errors. Z is computed from p, w and d only.
exposed:
What the view exposes:
- n_vars = n_opts = n (40, 50 or 100); n_groups = 1.
- ordered = True: positions are assigned in index order, position k being the k-th processed job.
- hard = [False]; detail = [False]: one soft group, the total weighted tardiness of the assigned prefix. For a complete answer this is the page's objective SUM w(j)T(j).
- capacity = int64 ones(n): each job once, so the answer is a permutation.
- var_attr = float64 (n, 0), empty: positions carry no attribute.
- opt_attr = float64 (n, 3): job i of the relabelled problem carries [p, w, d] of file job perm[i], taken from the instance's block in wt<n>.txt (n processing times, then n weights, then n due dates). This was checked equal to my own parse after decode's permutation.
- var_var, opt_opt, var_opt, occ_attr: empty tuples. domain, start_answer, start_totals: None.
- The state the learner holds has only a, used, tot and n. Arrays are read-only. The adapter object's own attributes are p, w and d only; problem() reads only inst['p'], inst['w'] and inst['d'].
- candidates() returns w(j)·max(t + p(j) - d(j), 0) for each unplaced job and 0 for placed ones. This is the exact change of the spec's partial total, not a hint.

Design decisions that shape difficulty but add nothing beyond the specification:
- Construction is strictly front to back; any other move needs a full evaluate() at n units.
- The elapsed time t is not exposed. It can be derived from the placed jobs' p, or from a tardy candidate's row.
- Every permutation is valid, so there is no hard group.
- No derived feature is given (no w/p, slack or ATC index), and no generation class (TF, RDD).
- Idle time is excluded. That loses nothing, since the objective never decreases when a completion time grows and every job is available at time 0.

Groups (TF, RDD per run of five) reach only the kernel's split.
